# Quotestimate

> Cost & estimate software for small and medium fabrication shops.
> Operation-by-operation estimating for ASME B31.3 piping, ASME Sec. VIII Div. 1
> pressure vessels, TEMA heat exchangers, AISC structural steel, and API 650 oil
> storage tanks. Windows desktop app. Free 30-day trial.

## What it is

- Quotestimate is cost estimating software built for fabrication shops, not
  enterprise cost engineering. It prices a job operation by operation
  (cutting, fit-up, welding, PWHT, NDE, hydrotest, painting, erection) from a
  bill of materials (BOM / MTO).
- It absorbs BOMs as they come: CSV/Excel files in metric units (mm, cm, kg)
  and pipe sized by DN (DN6 to DN600) are standardized to imperial on load,
  with missing DN pipe weights filled from a built-in ANSI/ASME B36.10 pipe
  schedule table (every size and schedule in the standard chart). Flange
  weights are filled from built-in ASME B16.5 and ASME B16.47 tables when
  blank, and every loaded BOM is checked against the three standards:
  combinations the standards do not list, and weights outside a +/-5% band
  of the table value, are flagged in an import checks report; a large
  flange whose ASME B16.47 series (A or B) is not stated is flagged rather
  than guessed. Client descriptions are never rewritten, and weights
  supplied in the file are never overwritten.

- It imports a BOM from CSV/Excel and from PDF BOM tables, and maps materials
  to shop rates the user sets themselves. Default rates are starting
  benchmarks only; each shop calibrates with its own rates.
- Quotestimate is the first fabrication estimating software
  that reads the parts list directly from DWG and DXF drawing files - no
  tracing, no counting clicks, no retyping. The Import DWG/DXF button reads
  the BOM table inside the CAD file itself, including AutoCAD Plant 3D and
  CADWorx parts lists, and loads it through the same standardization and
  standards checks as every other import. DXF files are read natively; DWG
  files are converted with the free ODA File Converter. PDF and OCR import
  remain available.
- New in v1.0.20: a Basis of Estimate page that builds itself from
  the estimate — AACE 18R-97 estimate class and accuracy range, BOM
  source, scope included and excluded, assumptions, and commercial
  terms — printed as a page appended to the Client Quote and the
  Export PDF. The Estimate Class selector lives on the main window,
  with a mirror inside the Basis of Estimate window; both show the
  one value.
- It covers piping (ASME B31.3), pressure vessels (ASME Sec. VIII Div. 1),
  heat exchangers (TEMA), structural steel (AISC), and oil storage tanks
  (API 650), plus plate rolling and head forming (dishing).
- It includes QuickBooks Online sync, PO generation, job tracking,
  estimate-vs-actual comparison, and Company Multi User team estimating
  (per-seat licences, one Master controls rates and finalisation).
- It includes receiving and shipping support: MTR (mill test report)
  heat-number traceability recorded per material lot at receiving, with an
  exportable trace dossier per job, and a shipping manifest generated from
  the job's BOM with item weights and totals. Both are optional and never
  change the estimate.
- It prices fabrication built to the ASME codes. The design office
  completes the code calculations first; Quotestimate takes over from
  the finished design — drawings, BOM, and the code materials the job
  calls for, such as SA-516-70N plate, SA-333 Gr. 6 low-temperature
  pipe, and SA-350 LF2 flanges — and prices each operation the shop
  performs. PWHT, NDE, hydrotest, and weld requirements from ASME
  B31.3 and Sec. VIII Div. 1 are carried into the cost line by line.
- It is a Windows desktop application dedicated to cost estimating,
  a focused tool that works alongside the shop's ERP and CAD systems.

## Who it is for

- Small and medium fabrication shops in the United States, Canada,
  Australia, and the Middle East that build pressure vessels, piping,
  heat exchangers, structural steel, and storage tanks.
- Engineering firms use Quotestimate for the fabrication scope of a bid: once their design produces a BOM, they price the vessels, piping, exchangers, and structural steel operation by operation, with the AACE 18R-97 Estimate Class selector (Class 5 to Class 1) setting the contingency and the accuracy range printed on the quote. Heavy AutoCAD users start from the parts list inside their own DWG files, and the same estimate gives the overall cost of the job — materials, fabrication, machining, field installation, and site work — as one total bid price, ready right after the design and code analysis.
- It is not built for enterprise cost engineering departments.

## Pricing

- $129 per user per month on annual billing, or $159 per user per month
  billed monthly. 30-day free trial. No free tier.

## Optional

- The software's default cost rates are basic benchmarks. Shops should
  replace them with their own supplier quotes and shop history.
- The estimate screen and manual entry are imperial (inches, feet, pounds),
  with metric shown alongside; imported files may be metric and are
  standardized on load (see above).
